title: B.Com Semester I — Pre-Assessment (Diagnostic)
subject: Commerce bridge (Accountancy, Business Studies, Economics)
scheme: Karnataka UG SEP 2024 / NEP 2020 — Sem I readiness
university: Bengaluru City University (template — substitute the college's affiliating university)
instructions: This is a diagnostic paper given in Week 1. It is not a university examination and does not count toward SEE.
It checks PUC / Class 12 Commerce readiness for B.Com Semester I (Financial Accounting, Marketing, Business Environment / Management).
Answer all questions in Sections A–D. Section E is one accounting problem.
Figures to the right of each question indicate marks.
Use a pen. Show working for the Section E problem.

sections.name: Accountancy
sections.instructions: Choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.text: The accounting equation is:
questions.explanation: Dual-aspect concept: every resource (asset) is financed by claims of owners (capital) and outsiders (liabilities).

questions.text: Under the golden rules of accounting, a Nominal account is debited when there is a:
questions.explanation: Nominal accounts: debit all expenses and losses; credit all incomes and gains.

questions.text: Which of the following is a current asset?
questions.explanation: Inventory is expected to be sold or consumed within the operating cycle, so it is a current asset.

questions.text: GST charged on goods purchased for resale is recorded as:

options.text: An expense of the business in all cases
Input tax credit (asset / recoverable) if the dealer is registered

questions.explanation: A registered dealer sets off GST paid on inward supplies (ITC) against GST collected on outward supplies.

questions.text: Depreciation is provided primarily because of the:
questions.explanation: The cost of a long-lived asset is allocated over the periods that benefit from it (matching), assuming the firm continues (going concern).

questions.text: A Trial Balance is prepared to:

options.text: Disclose the profit of the year
Check the arithmetical accuracy of ledger postings

questions.explanation: A trial balance lists debit and credit totals; agreement is evidence of arithmetical accuracy, not of a complete absence of errors.

questions.text: Purchase of a delivery van is:
questions.explanation: The van is a long-term asset that will generate benefits over several years — capital expenditure.

questions.text: In a bill of exchange, the person who writes and signs the bill is the:
questions.explanation: Drawer makes the bill; drawee is directed to pay; payee is entitled to receive.

questions.text: Under FIFO, closing stock is valued at:

options.text: The cost of the earliest purchases remaining
The cost of the most recent purchases remaining

questions.explanation: FIFO assumes oldest units are issued first, so stock is the latest lots.

questions.text: Which error will NOT be revealed by a trial balance?

options.text: Posting ₹5,000 to the debit of Rent instead of ₹500
Omitting to post one side of a journal entry
Complete omission of a transaction from the books
Casting a ledger account short on the debit side

questions.explanation: If both debit and credit are omitted equally, the trial balance still agrees. Unequal postings and wrong casts do not.

sections.name: Business Studies & Management
sections.instructions: Choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.text: Henri Fayol stated how many principles of management?
questions.explanation: Fayol's 14 principles (division of work, authority, discipline, unity of command, …, esprit de corps) are in the B.Com Sem I Management paper.

questions.text: Which sequence lists the core functions of management?
questions.explanation: POSDC (planning–organising–staffing–directing–controlling) is the standard Indian UG framing.

questions.text: Top-level management is primarily concerned with:

options.text: Strategic goals and policies of the organisation

questions.explanation: Board / MD / CEO set direction; middle managers translate it; first-line managers supervise operations.

questions.text: SWOC analysis is used mainly at the stage of:
questions.explanation: BCU Management Principles (Module 2) links SWOC to the planning / decision-making process.

questions.text: Unity of command means:

options.text: One plan for the whole organisation
A subordinate should receive orders from one superior only

questions.explanation: Unity of command ≠ unity of direction (one plan / one head for a group of activities).

questions.text: In Maslow's hierarchy, the need for respect and recognition is:
questions.explanation: Esteem sits above belongingness and below self-actualisation.

questions.text: A manager who takes decisions without consulting subordinates is using which leadership style?
questions.explanation: Autocratic = centralised authority; democratic = consultation; free-rein = high subordinate freedom.

questions.text: Which of the following is a part of the micro (task) environment of a firm?
questions.explanation: Micro / task environment: customers, suppliers, competitors, intermediaries. Macro: economic, political, legal, social, technological, natural.

questions.text: The minimum number of members required to form a public company in India is:
questions.explanation: Companies Act: private company ≥ 2 members; public company ≥ 7. (One-person company is a separate form.)

questions.text: F.W. Taylor is associated with:

options.text: Scientific management (time and motion, differential piece rate)

questions.explanation: Taylor = scientific management; Fayol = 14 principles; Maslow = needs; Herzberg = two-factor.

sections.name: Economics & Marketing
sections.instructions: Choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

questions.text: The law of demand, other things remaining the same, states that:

options.text: Price and quantity demanded move in the same direction
Price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions
Demand is always equal to supply

questions.explanation: Ceteris paribus, a higher price reduces quantity demanded (downward-sloping demand curve).

questions.text: GDP at market prices minus net indirect taxes equals:
questions.explanation: GDP_FC = GDP_MP − net indirect taxes (indirect taxes − subsidies).

questions.text: Which of the following is a function of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.unit: PUC Economics / SEP Indian Financial System

options.text: Collecting income tax from salaried employees
Issuing currency and acting as banker to the government

questions.explanation: RBI: note issue, banker/agent to government, banker to banks, monetary policy. Tax collection is CBDT/CBIC; Budget is Finance Ministry.

questions.text: Inflation is a sustained:

options.text: Fall in the general price level
Rise in the general price level
Rise in one commodity's price only

questions.explanation: Inflation = persistent rise in the general price level; deflation is the opposite.

questions.text: The four Ps of the marketing mix are:
questions.explanation: McCarthy's 4Ps. (Services marketing adds people, process, physical evidence — 7Ps.)

questions.text: Selling differs from marketing in that selling:

options.text: Starts with customer needs and designs the product around them
Focuses on converting existing output into cash
Is only used in online business

questions.explanation: Selling is inside-out (product → customer). Marketing is outside-in (customer need → product).

questions.text: Dividing a heterogeneous market into relatively homogeneous groups of buyers is called:
questions.explanation: Segmentation → targeting → positioning (STP). Bases: geographic, demographic, psychographic, behavioural.

questions.text: In the product life cycle, sales grow rapidly and competitors enter during:
questions.explanation: Introduction: low sales; growth: rapid sales + new rivals; maturity: peak; decline: falling sales.

questions.text: Under perfect competition, in the long run, firms typically earn:
questions.explanation: Free entry/exit drives economic profit to zero (normal profit) in the long run.

questions.text: A government budget deficit means:
questions.explanation: Budget deficit: spending > receipts. Trade deficit is exports vs imports — a different concept.

sections.name: Short answers
sections.instructions: Answer in 3–5 sentences or a short working. Each question carries 2 marks.

questions.text: State the accounting equation. If capital is ₹4,00,000 and liabilities are ₹1,50,000, compute assets.
Distinguish between a journal and a ledger (any two points).
questions.modelAnswer: Journal is the book of original entry recording transactions chronologically as debit/credit; ledger is the book of final entry where journal postings are classified account-wise. Journal answers 'what happened today'; ledger answers 'what is the balance of this account'.

questions.text: List any four of Fayol's principles of management.
questions.modelAnswer: Any four of: division of work, authority and responsibility, discipline, unity of command, unity of direction, subordination of individual interest, remuneration, centralisation, scalar chain, order, equity, stability of tenure, initiative, esprit de corps.

questions.text: What is market segmentation? Give two bases used to segment a consumer market.
questions.modelAnswer: Market segmentation is dividing a heterogeneous market into groups of buyers with similar needs or behaviour. Bases include geographic (region, urban/rural), demographic (age, income, gender), psychographic (lifestyle) and behavioural (loyalty, occasion).

questions.text: Name the three types of accounts in the traditional classification and state the debit rule for a Real account.
questions.modelAnswer: Personal, Real and Nominal. Real account: debit what comes in, credit what goes out.

questions.text:
From the following, prepare a Trading Account of Smt. Latha for the year ended 31 March 2026. Opening stock ₹40,000; Purchases ₹2,60,000; Purchase returns ₹10,000; Sales ₹4,20,000; Sales returns ₹20,000; Wages ₹18,000; Carriage inwards ₹7,000; Closing stock ₹55,000. (Ignore GST.)

Required: (a) show the Trading Account (8 marks); (b) state the gross profit or gross loss (2 marks).
questions.modelAnswer:
Dr Trading A/c Cr
To Opening stock 40,000
To Purchases 2,60,000 less returns 10,000 = 2,50,000
To Wages 18,000
To Carriage inwards 7,000
To Gross profit c/d 1,40,000
Total 4,55,000
By Sales 4,20,000 less returns 20,000 = 4,00,000
By Closing stock 55,000
Total 4,55,000
Gross profit = ₹1,40,000.
